title: What to expect when you write to me
subtitle: The whole arrangement, from first note to flight home - and the parts people don't expect.

text: No forms, no funnel, no sales script.
sub: The first exchange is a conversation about where you're leaning. Vague is fine - vague is how the good trips start.

items.head: You write
items.body: A region, a month, an occasion, a ship you half remember. That's plenty to start with.

items.head: I edit
items.body: A hundred possible sailings down to three worth your time, with a reason attached to each.

items.head: We settle it
items.body: Ship, cabin, deck, dining, the negotiated fare. You decide; I handle every booking detail.

items.head: I stay on it
items.body: The fare watched until you sail, the papers checked, and a person who answers if plans wobble.

sub: If a celebrated sailing is wrong for you, I'll say so before we ever speak about fares - that is most of the job.

quote: The line pays me after you sail. Your fare is the same or better - and my services are complimentary.

title: Send this to the person you'd sail with
body: Most voyages begin as a conversation between two people. When yours does, this is what writing to me starts.
